events.title: Washington Lays the Capitol Cornerstone
events.description: President George Washington laid the cornerstone of the United States Capitol in a Masonic ceremony. A parade came before it, and a celebration with feasting followed.
events.significance: The ceremony marked the start of construction on the building that became the home of the U.S. Congress and a lasting symbol of American democracy.

events.title: The New York Times Publishes Its First Issue
events.description: The first issue of the New-York Daily Times appeared on this day. The paper was later renamed The New York Times.
events.significance: The paper grew into one of the world's most influential news organizations and helped shape modern American journalism.

events.title: The Mukden Incident
events.description: Japanese army officers set off a small explosion near a railway line outside Mukden (now Shenyang) in Manchuria. They blamed Chinese saboteurs and used the staged incident as a pretext to attack.
events.significance: It led to Japan's occupation of Manchuria. Many historians see it as the start of the conflict that grew into World War II in Asia.

events.title: The National Security Act Takes Effect
events.description: The main provisions of the National Security Act of 1947 took effect on this day. They created the Central Intelligence Agency and the National Security Council, and the act also paved the way for a separate U.S. Air Force.
events.significance: The act restructured the American military and intelligence systems for the Cold War, and its institutions still shape U.S. foreign policy.
